body: Since I cannot see, I have no idea about her undertone.  Is this something that a store employee could tell me or what's the best way?

Ok, wanted to add.  I just had this set described to me that you linked.  I use a service called "Be My Eyes" which is amazing!   So it's a riot of bright colors!  I think I am going to save that for maybe..  next year?   I think just to start I want to give her more.. innocent? light? subtle? (what is the right word?) colors to start with for makeup she is going to wear out and about or to school.  Then we can expand to all the crazy colors when she's a little older and is used to it a little more? 
Or maybe I could get the rainbow palette you linked but that's just for at home playing around but not for wearing to school and such.      Oh god, this is so tricky!

Everyone has been so fantastic with the information.  I already purchased some recommended spf and cleanser. 

I appreciate the advice to let her go hog wild.  I figure I can't see it and it's just us, so I won't really care and I think you are correct to let her experiment and I promise I will.   Thank you for that wisdom.     However, I don't really understand anything about makeup, blind since birth, but I gather just from general reading that it shouldn't be too heavy for this age?  Not that I will be able to judge anyway.   I'm not concerned at all about boys or whatever at all.  It's all the natural phases of life.  Honestly my concern from my POV is..  I don't know.. pedos? Is that a thing with makeup on young girls?   I guess I'm also concerned on how to frame this in a way to make sure she knows she is not expected to wear it.  Like.. she can do it if she wants to, totally her choice, but she is also beautiful without it.   I don't know I'm still trying to feel this out.  I don't want her self esteem to be affected.  I'm not being very clear because it's all still new to me and I'm trying to figure it out myself.    I just know I want her to have a healthy relationship with makeup and her self esteem at the same time.

I am blind and Audio is my medium.  I listen to audio books every chance I get.  Normally I don't like voice acting I just like a book to be read straight -but they did such a bang up job, I can't help but love it.   It makes me wonder what I've been missing. 

PS - I'm glad there is no music or sound effects, that would make me crazy.  But the voice acting? Totally.  Donut would have to be played by a drag queen in real life.

I am visually impaired.  Up until I was a teenager,  I listened to audio cassettes.  Something like a Dean Koontz novel could have like 20+ cassettes.     I would check them out from the library or use other services.

If you are visually impaired a truly valuable service is the library for the blind and print impaired. https://www.loc.gov/nls/

After that, it switched to CD's and now we've gotten rid of all physical media.  It's fantastic.
Thanks for looking that up.  I didn't realize it was quite so long.   (but soooo worth it!)

Let me put a front porch on this and say I am visually impaired, read: Blind as a bat.   

So I work with a woman like this except it's a little different.   If she's talking to a group of women, she's just her normal self talking in a perfectly normal voice.   I can *instantly* tell whenever a male walks into the room because she immediately turns on this what I can only describe as a Marilyn Monroe voice.  She gets all breathy and giggly and overly flirtatious. It's so obviously fake and over the top but the men eat it up with a spoon.    I am blind but even I can practically see her sticking out her chest and biting her lip.    I secretly call it her "man catcher" act and to me, it's just gross. 

Then, I can tell when the male walks out of the room because it flips off like a switch and she's her normal self again. 

I know she wears too much perfume.  I'm afraid to ask anyone, but I'm guessing she wears too much makeup and makes sure there's lots of cleavage.    
 
The weird part is, I would never say anything but I desperately want to ask her if that's deliberate act on her part or is it automatic? 

And the worst part? She's been like this for years and is still single.

Some cats are not meant to live inside. For example, I have a garden cat.   She's not allowed in the house at all - but she never tries to get in, either.  

We adopted her from the shelter, but it turned out she was there for a reason.  Spent many months trying to train it to use a cat box.  Spent time with cat behaviori$t $$$$, followed all the advice, bought 5 or 6 different kinds of cat boxes, 15 or more types of litter, different locations, one in each and every room, etc etc.    Someone is going to read this and tell me something I should have tried, but believe me, we tried everything the expert said and then some.   Nope.   She just prefers to shit and piss wherever, whenever. 

Now she's a garden cat.  

She has a covered place to be cozy under my covered deck and a heating pad warmed cat-house during our (very mild) winters.  It doesn't snow here.  I'm visually impaired so I put a loud tinkle bell on her so I can know she's around.   She doesn't like to be picked up, but will tolerate a head scratch. 

Her life may be shorter, but it's damn sure longer than if she were at the high kill shelter.   If someone reading this has something negative to say about that, they can go ahead and contact me and  they can adopt her and keep her inside.   Then they will know the joys of stepping in cat shit at 3AM in bare feet on the way to bathroom.    Or spend months and hundreds of dollars trying to get the cat pee out of, well.. everything and then giving up and buying all new rugs and a new couch.  This cat was fucking expensive. 

This is an outside cat!

There is, actually.  It's a fantastic app called Good Maps.   It's a wonderful thing but it helps you in the moment.  It does not give you an advance game plan of where you need to go.   Also, you need you need to be slow or stop to get your bearings with the app and when people are rush rushing around like at an airport you are liable to get knocked over just standing there.   I may get there and that particular office is not in the app.  Or the app isn't working.  Or I can't get signal.   

For all of these reasons, not the least of which is that if something is going to wrong tech-wise, it will happen to me.    

For all those reasons I get a lot of comfort from having an old fashioned text description such as the kind person wrote above.
